elements.problem: Encoded as (<= (onset Diarrhea) (time_ago 2 weeks)). If onset is a timestamp compared to the timestamp 'now minus 2 weeks', <= means the onset was 2 or more weeks ago, i.e. duration >= 2 weeks: the opposite of the page's '<= 2 weeks'. The page's branch needs onset within the last 2 weeks, i.e. (>= (onset ...) (time_ago 2 weeks)). The grammar does not document the direction, so confirm against the VHA evaluator; if it is reversed, the dysentery, gastroenteritis and cholera-by-flowchart rules all fire on chronic diarrhoea instead of acute. Also, duration is never asked (no check_for).

summary: The most consequential risk is the duration guard (<= (onset Diarrhea) (time_ago 2 weeks)), which probably encodes 'started 2 or more weeks ago'. That would invert the <= 2 weeks branch for dysentery, gastroenteritis and flowchart cholera, and duration is never asked for anyway. The urgent box is otherwise well structured but loses the 5-day window on cholera exposure and footnote 1's shock criteria, and the faecal impaction rules drop the > 65 years trigger.
